takeaway: Over half of a humanoid's motors move its legs and keep it balanced, hands with fingers need about as many again, and the battery limits how long it can work.

selfCheck.question: What stops a humanoid working a full shift today?
selfCheck.answer: The battery stops it. One charge lasts only about two hours, which is much shorter than a work shift, so it would stop partway through unless a person swapped in a charged battery.

sentence: A humanoid robot needs a motor at each joint to move. Most of the G1's motors are in its legs, because the legs hold up and balance the whole body. Hands with fingers would need about as many motors again. The battery inside the chest lasts only about two hours.
unclearTerms: "Waist: 1 motor" vs answer "torso has no motors" (contradiction)
"fixed, with no motors" (can't move at all?)

reason: My takeaway says the same three things: most motors are in the legs because they hold up and balance the body, hands with fingers need about as many again, and the roughly two-hour battery limits how long it can work.
